text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 > 2.5s). Auto-paging to #incidents. Please ack if oncall.

devin: acked. I'm oncall. seeing spike starting ~1834567200, correlated with increased preproc CPU on preproc-prod-*.

sarah: I'm joining. any customer-facing errors?

support_amelia: Support telemetry: 4 customers saw streaming stalls (clients reported partial responses then stall) — ticket ids: T-4821, T-4822. No 5xxs, just timeouts on client side after 10s.

ops_jay: metrics: p95 jumped from 280ms -> 520ms, p99 ~2.7s. Input rate stable. Backend GPU utilization normal. Preproc service CPU at 92% and queue depth spiked.

ml_kate: throwing early hypothesis: template rendering + JSON mode change pushed more tokens into tokenizer and disabled prefix caching on some flows. Recent PR merged: render-engine@v2.1.4 (rolled 4h ago).

eng_tom: timeline: deploy render-engine v2.1.4 at 1834566000. Preproc autoscaler didn't kick until queue > 120s. Looks like CPU-bound sync work in prompt construction.

devin: can you dump traces from preproc for a slow request?

eng_tom: attaching sample span (sanitized):
```
span: preproc.render_template  duration=1024ms
span: preproc.tokenize        duration=320ms
span: preproc.jsonmode.parse duration=480ms
span: preproc.kv_cache.lookup duration=12ms
```

ops_jay: spot on — render_template now does more work (schema expansion loops). This increases tokens BEFORE KV cache hits so prefix cache miss rate up.

ml_kate: impact on streaming: tokenizer stall delays first token to runtime -> streaming obs shows 'first_token_latency' jumps and later tokens stream but with gaps. That matches customer reports.

devin: mitigation plan (short): 1) roll back render-engine -> v2.1.3, 2) enable temporary rate limit for JSON-mode requests, 3) reroute high-latency traffic to fallback model pool (smaller context model). Who can run rollback?

sarah: I'll coordinate rollback. rolling immediately to v2.1.3 on preproc-prod canary, then global if green.

eng_tom: running rollback on canary now: `kubectl set image deploy/preproc render-engine=render-engine:v2.1.3 --namespace=prod`

incident-bot: deploy-bot: started job deploy/preproc-rollout-1834568100

ops_jay: also enabling prefix KV cache fallback: set `PREPROC_PREFIX_CACHE=on` for all preproc pods via feature flag; this will trade memory for lower tokenization cost. Applying now.

support_amelia: messaging note: pinging impacted customers with status update. ETA for full mitigation?

devin: after canary 5m observation, if p99 drops <1s we'll scale gradually back to normal and lift rate limit. ETA 15-25m.

eng_tom: canary status: preproc-canary logs show render_template duration down to 240ms, tokenize 90ms. promoting rollout.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete for render-engine:v2.1.3 (success) — rollout_id=deploy/preproc-rollout-1834568100, duration=8m

ops_jay: metrics now: p95 310ms, p99 680ms, queue depth back to baseline. Streaming first-token latency reduced.

ml_kate: follow-up: create ticket to re-evaluate render-engine performance for large tool schemas and JSON mode. Action items: add unit test for template expansion path, restore prefix cache invariants, and add pre-deploy perf test that simulates heavy schema expansion.

devin: noted. Also set temporary alert: preproc.render_template > 500ms -> pager.

support_amelia: I posted customer updates and closed two support tickets with mitigation link. Third customer still has flaky client timeouts; support working with them.

sarah: oncall handover in 2h. I'll leave notes in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1834567890 (doc draft).

eng_tom: root cause: render-engine v2.1.4 introduced synchronous schema expansion in the main path for JSON-mode prompts which dramatically increased CPU/time spent before tokenizer cache could be used. Regression in perf path.

ml_kate: long term: explore async template expansion or incremental streaming of prompt hydration so we can start tokenization earlier. Also add regression tests that measure preproc end-to-end p99 under synthetic schema blowup.

devin: thanks team. marking incident as mitigated for now; will keep thread open for postmortem and RCA. :white_check_mark:
